title: Repair
contents: property | Requires | Repair toolkit; stable surface; both hands
text | Attempt Crafting to fix a damaged item. The GM sets the DC, usually its Craft DC. Destroyed items cannot be Repaired. Training is not required.
text | Critical success: Restore 10 HP + 10 per Crafting proficiency rank.
text | Success: Restore 5 HP + 5 per rank. Failure: No change. Critical failure: Deal 2d6 damage to the item, reduced by its Hardness.
text | Ranks: untrained 0, trained 1, expert 2, master 3, legendary 4. At trained: 20 HP on critical success; 10 HP on success.
text | Quick Repair changes the time only if you actually have that feat.

title: Hack
contents: property | Cost | Exploration; time set by GM
property | Requires | Trained Computers; hacking toolkit
text | Attempt Computers to access, control, or change an active secured system. The system sets the DC and may require multiple successes.
text | Critical success: Access it, or gain 2 successes; leave no trace.
text | Success: Access it, or gain 1 success.
text | Failure: No progress; some systems activate security measures.
text | Critical failure: Activate special security protocols or become locked out. A lockout prevents another access attempt for 1 hour.
text | Hack is for security; repairing broken hardware is a different task. Combat Hack is a separate feat.

title: Operate Device
contents: property | Requires | Use a computer or similar device
text | Use Computers to perform a task with a digital device. Training is not required; the GM sets a DC when a check is needed.
text | Critical success: Excel, learning secrets or advanced functionality.
text | Success: Operate it successfully and obtain general information.
text | Failure: Cannot understand it; −2 circumstance penalty to further attempts to access or play it for the next day.
text | Critical failure: Make a mistake preventing access to the program for the next day.
text | An accessible interface does not automatically require Hack.

title: Disable a Device
contents: property | Requires | Trained Thievery; trained Computers for computerized devices
text | Disarm a trap or complex device. Use Thievery, or Computers for a computerized device. The GM or device specifies the DC, successes needed, and any higher training requirement.
text | An infiltrator’s toolkit is useful and may be required for a physical device; other access or tools depend on the device.
text | Critical success: Disable it or gain 2 successes. Leave no trace and can rearm it later if possible.
text | Success: Disable it or gain 1 success. Failure: No progress. Critical failure: Trigger it.
text | Environmental hazards can have their own listed methods instead.

title: Pick a Lock
contents: property | Requires | Trained Thievery; infiltrator’s toolkit worn or held
text | Attempt Thievery against the lock’s DC. Locks can require several successful attempts.
text | Critical success: Open it, or gain 2 successes toward opening it. Leave no trace.
text | Success: Open it, or gain 1 success. Close inspection reveals evidence of picking.
text | Critical failure: Break your toolkit and leave obvious damage. Repair the toolkit or replace its picks (3 credits; 30 for tactical picks).
text | This does not itself grant control of a vehicle or defeat every electronic security system.

title: Administer First Aid
contents: property | Requires | Medkit worn or held; adjacent dying or bleeding creature
text | Attempt Medicine; training is not required. Choose one treatment if the target is both dying and bleeding.
text | Stabilize: Target must have 0 HP and dying. DC = 5 + recovery DC (usually 15 + dying value). Success removes dying but leaves it unconscious at 0 HP. Critical failure increases dying by 1.

text | Stop bleeding: Usually check against the DC of the effect causing persistent bleed. Success grants assisted recovery with the lower flat-check DC for particularly appropriate help. Critical failure immediately deals its persistent bleed damage.
text | Failure has no effect. This action does not restore HP.

title: Treat Wounds
contents: property | Requires | Trained Medicine; medkit worn or held
text | Treat one injured living creature, including yourself. Normally attempt DC 15 Medicine.
text | Critical success: Restore 4d8 HP and remove wounded. Success: Restore 2d8 HP and remove wounded. Failure: No healing. Critical failure: Deal 1d8 damage.
text | Target is immune to Treat Wounds for 1 hour from the start of treatment. On success, continue to a total of 1 hour to double the HP restored.
text | Optional higher DCs: expert DC 20 (+10 HP); master DC 30 (+30 HP); legendary DC 40 (+50 HP). These bonuses apply to successful healing, not critical-failure damage.

title: Make an Impression
contents: property | Requires | Conversation; no training required
text | Attempt Diplomacy vs. Will DC after friendly conversation. Choose one target, or up to five targets with a −2 penalty. Circumstances can modify the check.
text | Critical success: Attitude improves 2 steps. Success: Improves 1 step. Failure: No change. Critical failure: Worsens 1 step.
text | The change normally lasts for this social interaction. Attitudes: hostile → unfriendly → indifferent → friendly → helpful.
text | This improves attitude; use Request to ask for a specific favor. Apply Group Impression if you have it.

title: Request
contents: property | Requires | A friendly or helpful creature
text | Ask for something the target could accept given its attitude. Attempt Diplomacy against a DC set by the GM. Training is not required.
text | Success: Agrees, possibly with conditions or changes.
text | Failure: Refuses, perhaps offering a less extreme alternative.
text | Critical failure: Refuses and its attitude worsens 1 step.
text | Even helpful creatures will not accept some requests. Ordinary conversation does not require a check for every question.

title: Gather Information
contents: property | Requires | Access to people; no training required
text | Ask around local gathering places about an individual or topic. The GM sets the time and DC for a secret Diplomacy check.
text | Success: Learn information the GM provides. Failure: No useful information. Critical failure: Collect misinformation.
text | Bribes, drinks, or gifts may help as the GM determines. Apply Hobnobber if you have it.
text | Talking to one known contact can simply be a conversation; this activity is for canvassing an area.

title: Demoralize
contents: property | Requires | Aware of a creature within 30 feet
text | Attempt Intimidation vs. Will DC. Training is not required.
text | Take a −4 circumstance penalty if the target does not understand your language or you are not speaking a language.
text | Critical success: Frightened 2. Success: Frightened 1. Failure has no effect.
text | Regardless of outcome, that target is immune to your Demoralize for 10 minutes.

text | Frightened imposes a status penalty equal to its value on all checks and DCs, including AC. Normally decrease it by 1 at the end of the creature’s turn. This does not compel surrender or obedience.

title: Coerce
contents: property | Requires | Conversation; no training required
text | Threaten a creature, then attempt Intimidation vs. Will DC, adjusted for circumstances.
text | Critical success: Gives information or follows directions unlikely to harm it, for a GM-set duration up to 1 day. Then becomes unfriendly, but is too afraid to retaliate in the short term.
text | Success: As above, but it may retaliate afterward.
text | Failure: Refuses and becomes unfriendly unless already worse. Critical failure: Refuses, becomes hostile, and is immune to your Coercion for at least 1 week.
text | Quick Coercion shortens the conversation only if you have that feat. Coerce is not a combat command.

title: Lie
contents: text | Tell an untruth. Elaborate lies take longer. The GM resolves a secret Deception check against each listener’s Perception DC, with circumstance adjustments.
text | Failure: It disbelieves you and gains +4 circumstance bonus against your further lies for the conversation; it is more likely to distrust you later.
text | Implausible claims are harder or impossible to believe. New contradictory evidence can prompt a later Sense Motive check.
text | Apply Charming Liar only if you have that feat and meet its conditions.

title: Area Fire
contents: property | Requires | Wielding a weapon with the area trait
text | Attack the weapon’s designated area. A cone or line reaches its range increment. For a burst, place its center anywhere within the first range increment and use its listed radius.
text | Every creature in the area makes a basic Reflex save against your class DC + the weapon’s tracking value. You do not roll an attack roll.

text | Critical success: no damage; success: half damage; failure: full damage; critical failure: double damage. Critical failures also trigger applicable critical-hit effects, including weapon critical specialization.
text | This is area damage and spends ammunition equal to the weapon’s expend. Allies in the area are affected too.
